_note: v2 hook overrides for l'observatoire & météo (B32_ciel). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text (or that name a printed sign or a brewery), so the card always describes what is in the picture.

fr_tempete_noun.hook: Like English 'tempest', said tahn-PEHT: a STORM blows so hard that somebody's PET poodle floats up over the weather station like a fluffy kite.
fr_tempete_noun.why: The painting shows the poodle floating up on its own, without its owner.

fr_brouillard_noun.hook: Sounds like 'brew-yard' ("broo-YAHR"): a friendly witch stirs her bubbling green BREW, and thick FOG pours out of the cauldron until the whole YARD is lost in FOG.
fr_brouillard_noun.why: owner review: a witch's brew fogging the yard replaces the shivering boy Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (broo-YAR -> broo-YAHR).

fr_tonnerre_noun.hook: THUNDER: a gray cloud drops a huge iron weight that lands with a BOOM, a TON ("to") of noise in the air ("NAIR").
fr_tonnerre_noun.why: The painting turns the 'ton of noise' into a real one-ton weight dropping from a cloud.

fr_foudre_noun_f.hook: A bolt of LIGHTNING strikes a little food ("FOODR") truck and makes it sparkle.
fr_foudre_noun_f.why: Paintings carry no text, so the truck has no sign to light up.

fr_prevision_noun.hook: Like English 'prevision' (seeing ahead), said pray-vee-ZYOHN: a crystal ball shows tomorrow's FORECAST: sunshine, then a cloud shaped like a sheep.
fr_prevision_noun.why: The painting shows the crystal ball by itself, to avoid a second girl next to the girl with cloud hair.

fr_univers_noun.hook: Like English 'universe', said ew-nee-VEHR: a UNIcycle rolls through the UNIVERSE with a bunch of little galaxies squeezed together on its one seat, all sharing the ride.
fr_univers_noun.why: owner review: a unicycle shared by a bunch of galaxies replaces the rubber duck

fr_lune_noun.hook: Like English 'lunar', said LEWN: a LOON bird sings to the full MOON from the roof of a little stone tower.
fr_lune_noun.why: The painting puts the loon on a stone tower in the star garden, not on the observatory.

fr_galaxie_noun.hook: Like English 'galaxy', said gah-lahk-SEE: a GALAXY swirls across the night sky like a SEA of glitter.
fr_galaxie_noun.why: The painting shows the galaxy in the open sky rather than on a planetarium dome.

fr_secheresse_noun.hook: In a DROUGHT a scarecrow in a sash dress ("saysh-REHS") stands over cracked, DRY earth beside a wilting sunflower.
fr_secheresse_noun.why: The painted scarecrow stands by the sunflower without a fan.

fr_gel_noun.hook: Like English 'gel' (as in GELatin), said ZHEHL: a hard FROST has set the weather hut inside a giant clear, wobbly block of frozen GELatin, sparkling with ice crystals; a wisp from its chimney still curls out of the top.
fr_gel_noun.why: owner review: the frost needs gelatin

fr_ouragan_noun.hook: Sounds like 'Oregon' ("oo-rah-GAHN"): a HURRICANE swirls down onto a big map of the state of OREGON lying on the grass, covering its pine forests and snowy volcano.
fr_ouragan_noun.why: owner review: Oregon covered by a hurricane

fr_mistral_noun.hook: Like English 'mistral', said mees-TRAHL: the MISTRAL wind streams MISS Molly's long scarf out behind her as she battles down the TRAIL.
fr_mistral_noun.why: The painting shows the scarf flying in the wind; her hat and shopping list stay put.

fr_meteorologique_adj.hook: Like English 'meteorological', said may-tay-oh-roh-loh-ZHEEK: a weather scientist in round spectacles and a white coat checks her METEOROLOGICAL instruments, a wind vane and a rain gauge, and notes them on her clipboard.
fr_meteorologique_adj.why: The painted instrument stand has a wind vane and a rain gauge but no thermometer. The owl in spectacles is now a woman scientist. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook.

fr_lancement_noun.hook: A toy rocket LAUNCH ("lahn-suh"): it whooshes up from a little launch pad on the hill.
fr_lancement_noun.why: The painting sets the toy launch outdoors beside the observatory.

fr_astronome_noun.hook: Like English 'astronomer', said ahs-troh-NOM: an ASTRONOMER in a woolly hat peers through a big brass telescope at a comet.
fr_astronome_noun.why: The painting has only one garden gnome (le nain), so the astronomer is drawn as a person.

fr_eclair_noun.hook: Like the pastry's name ÉCLAIR (ay-KLEHR): a LIGHTNING bolt zaps down from a little storm cloud onto a chocolate éclair on the grass, which crackles with sparks. Here un éclair is the FLASH OF LIGHTNING.
fr_eclair_noun.why: RECS 1.4: weather sense; the pastry is a separate entry (fr_eclair_noun_2, bakery).

fr_atmosphere_noun.hook: Like English 'atmosphere', said aht-mohs-FEHR: the ATMOSPHERE is a huge glowing glass SPHERE of air, and a rocket blasts across inside it with a very surprised seagull clinging to its nose.
fr_atmosphere_noun.why: owner review: the atmosphere should involve a sphere

fr_spatial_adj.hook: Sounds like 'spatial, y'all' ("spah-SYAHL"): in the round SPACE station a cat in a cowboy hat tips its hat at you and drawls 'Howdy, Y'ALL!'
fr_spatial_adj.why: owner review: cowboy-hat cat saying y'all

fr_globe_noun.hook: Like English 'globe', said GLOB: a giant GLOBE stands on the headland with a big blue GLOB of goo dripping off its North Pole.
fr_globe_noun.why: painting shows the goo blob on the globe, no child

fr_soleil_noun.hook: The SUN lounges in a striped deckchair, SO LAZY: soh-LEHY = so la(zy).
fr_soleil_noun.why: painting shows the sun in a deckchair, not on a nest

fr_neige_noun.hook: SNOW piles high on a bird's NEST ("nezh"), and a little bird peeps out of the snowy nest.
fr_neige_noun.why: The bird no longer wears earmuffs; it is a plain bird. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook.

fr_satellite_noun.hook: Like English 'satellite', said sah-tay-LEET: a SATELLITE blinks its LIGHT as it passes over, and an owl flaps past it.
fr_satellite_noun.why: The owl just flies (no waving). Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook.

fr_eternite_noun.hook: Like English 'eternity', said ay-tehr-nee-TAY: a snail sets off along the stepping stones across the sky dome, a trip that will take an ETERNITY.
fr_eternite_noun.why: No packed lunch is painted, and the snail stays a plain snail. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook.

fr_verglas_noun.hook: A road covered in BLACK ICE ("vehr-GLAH") is as slippery as very glass; a penguin toboggans across it on its belly.
fr_verglas_noun.why: The penguin slides on its belly like a real penguin instead of skating like a person. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ver-GLAH -> vehr-GLAH).

fr_lunaire_adj.hook: Like English 'lunar', said lew-NEHR: a LUNAR landscape: a little girl astronaut in a spacesuit leaps past the cratered moon.
fr_lunaire_adj.why: The rabbit in a spacesuit is now a girl astronaut. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook.

fr_pole_noun.hook: Like English 'pole', said POHL: a little girl explorer in a blue parka plants a flag on the South POLE while a penguin looks on.
fr_pole_noun.why: A child plants the flag; the penguin is a plain penguin. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook.

fr_bise_noun.en: north wind; also: a kiss on the cheek (faire la bise)
fr_bise_noun.hook: "BEEZ": two BEES cling to the old stump as the cold NORTH WIND, la bise, blows them sideways.
fr_bise_noun.why: RECS 1.4: weather room = the north wind; the kissing bees were repainted as bees braced against the wind.

fr_canicule_noun.hook: "CAN-EE-COOL" ("kah-nee-KEWL"): on the cracked dry ground a sweltering girl tips a watering CAN of COOL water over her head; the thermometer beside her bursts out of the top. A HEATWAVE.
fr_canicule_noun.why: Moved from horloge (1.2 B/C); weather room. Painting shows exactly this.

fr_orage_noun.hook: A THUNDERSTORM with orange ("oh-RAHZH") lightning crashes over the village.
fr_orage_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (o-RAZH -> oh-RAHZH).

fr_ciel_noun.hook: Look up at the SKY: you can see an L-shaped ("SYEHL") cloud floating in the blue.
fr_ciel_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (SYEL -> SYEHL).
